what: 🦠 Step 1 — Crop and disease calibration on selected sowing dates
title: Wheat blast on wheat in Brazil
text: published analysis, crop disease parameters calibrated together (calibration = "") three sowing dates, remaining sowing dates kept validation. 👉 idea : Select subset sowing dates (planting periods 1, 5 10, article) calibration. crop, calibrate cycle length, flowering start radiation use efficiency. wheat blast, start default parameters settings used article. Run franchestyn separately planting period. Collect estimated crop disease parameters run. Average across planting periods rebuild consistent parameter sets. average across planting periods: Snapshot calibrated disease parameters stage, calibCrop calibDisease contain crop epidemiological parameters averaged across calibration sowing dates. reduces noise single calibrations provides robust baseline validation remaining experiments.
code: # -------------------------------------------------------------- # 📌 Step 1: Crop + disease calibration on selected sowing dates # --------------------------------------------------------------  # 1. Load the Brazil wheat parameter set bundled with the package data("cropParameters_brazil")  # 2. Crop: calibrate only phenology and radiation use efficiency thisCropParam <- FraNchEstYN::disable_all_calibration(cropParameters_brazil) thisCropParam$CycleLength$calibration            <- TRUE thisCropParam$CycleLength$min                    <- 1500 thisCropParam$CycleLength$max                    <- 2500 thisCropParam$RadiationUseEfficiency$calibration <- TRUE thisCropParam$FloweringStart$calibration         <- TRUE  # 3. Disease: default wheat blast parameters, with the settings used in the article thisDiseaseParam <- diseaseParameters$wheat_blast thisDiseaseParam$SenescenceAcceleratorDamage$calibration <- FALSE thisDiseaseParam$SenescenceAcceleratorDamage$value       <- 0 thisDiseaseParam$SenescenceAcceleratorDamage$max         <- 0.5 thisDiseaseParam$LightStealerDamage$calibration          <- FALSE thisDiseaseParam$LightStealerDamage$value                <- 0 thisDiseaseParam$AssimilateSappersDamage$value           <- 0 thisDiseaseParam$AssimilateSappersDamage$calibration     <- TRUE thisDiseaseParam$CyclePercentageOnset$min                <- 20 thisDiseaseParam$OuterInoculumShapeRelease$value         <- 1 thisDiseaseParam$OuterInoculumShapeParameter$value       <- 0 thisDiseaseParam$IsSplashBorne$value                     <- 0  # 4. Study period and calibration sowing dates start_end <- c(2011, 2020) pps <- c(1, 5, 10)  all_parameters_crop    <- list() all_parameters_disease <- list()  # 5. Calibrate on each planting period for (pp in pps) {    df <- FraNchEstYN::franchestyn(     weather_data      = weather_data,     management_data   = management_brazil |> filter(planting_period == pp),     reference_data    = reference_brazil  |> filter(planting_period == pp),     cropParameters    = thisCropParam,     diseaseParameters = thisDiseaseParam,     calibration       = "all",     # crop + disease     start_end         = start_end,     iterations        = 999        # simplex iterations   )    all_parameters_crop[[length(all_parameters_crop) + 1]] <-     parameters_to_df(df$parameters$crop) |> mutate(planting_period = pp)   all_parameters_disease[[length(all_parameters_disease) + 1]] <-     parameters_to_df(df$parameters$disease) |> mutate(planting_period = pp) }  # 6. Merge the calibrations from all planting periods parameters_df_crop <- dplyr::bind_rows(all_parameters_crop,    .id = "run_id") parameters_df      <- dplyr::bind_rows(all_parameters_disease, .id = "run_id") # 7. Mean, standard deviation and sample size across planting periods summarise_params <- function(x) {   x %>%     group_by(Parameter) %>%     summarise(       value    = mean(as.numeric(Value), na.rm = TRUE),       sd_value = sd(as.numeric(Value),   na.rm = TRUE),       n        = sum(!is.na(Value)),       .groups  = "drop"     ) } param_summary_crop <- summarise_params(parameters_df_crop) param_summary      <- summarise_params(parameters_df)  # 8. Rebuild parameter lists with the averaged values (±20% range) #    and switch calibration off for the validation runs calibCrop    <- FraNchEstYN::df_to_parameters(param_summary_crop, range_pct = 0.2) |>   FraNchEstYN::disable_all_calibration() calibDisease <- FraNchEstYN::df_to_parameters(param_summary, range_pct = 0.2) |>   FraNchEstYN::disable_all_calibration()

Initialize empty list to store all simulation outputs outputsSim <- list()  # Fungicide: protectant; these are the package default values (fungicideParameters$protectant), set a priori as in the article fungicideParam <- FraNchEstYN::disable_all_calibration(FraNchEstYN::fungicideParameters$protectant) fungicideParam$TenacityFactor$value  <- 0.05 fungicideParam$DegradationRate$value <- 0.02 fungicideParam$InitialEfficacy$value <- 1 fungicideParam$AShapeParameter$value <- 3 fungicideParam$BShapeParameter$value <- 8  # no further calibration, just simulate       start_end           = c(2012, 2014)     )      # If simulation produced outputs, store them in the list     if (!is.null(res$outputs$simulation)) {       outputsSim[[paste(thisScheduling$site, var, thisScheduling$fungicide, sep = "_")]] <-         res$outputs$simulation %>%         mutate(site = thisScheduling$site, variety = var,                fungicide = thisScheduling$fungicide)     }   } }  #
